verses.zh: 不知羞耻的国民哪，你们应当聚集！趁命令没有发出，日子过去如风前的糠，耶和华的烈怒未临到你们，他发怒的日子未到以先，你们应当聚集前来。
verses.en: Bunch yourselves together like straw,[NOTE:1] you undesirable[NOTE:2] nation,
notes: The Hebrew text combines a Hitpolel imperative of קָשַׁשׁ (qashash) with a Qal imperative of the same root. Elsewhere this root appears in the polel stem with the meaning “gather stubble.” Zephaniah’s command is ironic, implying the people are like stubble or straw. As such, they are vulnerable to the Lord’s fiery judgment that will quickly consume them (see 1:18). See Adele Berlin, Zephaniah (AB 25A), 96.

Some relate this word to an Aramaic cognate meaning “to be ashamed.” With the negative particle it would then mean “unashamed” (cf. NIV “shameful”; NRSV “shameless”). However, elsewhere in biblical Hebrew the verb means “to desire,” or with the negative particle “undesirable.” Cf. also NEB “unruly.”

verses.en: before God’s decree becomes reality[NOTE:1] and the day of opportunity disappears like windblown chaff,[NOTE:2] before the Lord’s raging anger[NOTE:3] overtakes[NOTE:4] you—before the day of the Lord’s angry judgment overtakes you!
notes: Heb “before the giving birth of a decree.” For various alternative readings, see J. J. M. Roberts, Nahum, Habakkuk, and Zephaniah (OTL), 187-88.

The second half of the line reads literally, “like chaff it passes by a day.” The translation above assumes the “day” is the brief time God is giving the nation to repent. The comparison of this quickly passing opportunity to chaff is consistent with the straw imagery of v. 1.
Heb “the fury of the anger of the Lord.” The synonyms are combined to emphasize the extreme degree of the Lord’s anger.
Heb “comes upon.” This phrase occurs twice in this verse.

verses.zh: 世上遵守耶和华典章的谦卑人哪，你们都当寻求耶和华！当寻求公义谦卑，或者在耶和华发怒的日子可以隐藏起来。
verses.en: Seek the Lord’s favor,[NOTE:1] all you humble people[NOTE:2] of the land who have obeyed his commands![NOTE:3] Strive to do what is right![NOTE:4] Strive to be humble![NOTE:5] Maybe you will be protected[NOTE:6] on the day of the Lord’s angry judgment.
notes: Heb “seek the Lord,” but “favor” seems to be implied from the final line of the verse.
Or “poor.” The precise referent of this Hebrew term is unclear. The word may refer to the economically poor or to the spiritually humble.

The present translation assumes the Hebrew term מִשְׁפָּט (mishpat) here refers to God’s covenantal requirements and is a synonym for the Law. The word can mean “justice” and could refer more specifically to the principles of justice contained in the Law. In this case the phrase could be translated, “who have promoted the justice God demands.”
Heb “Seek what is right.”
Heb “Seek humility.”
Heb “hidden.” Cf. NEB “it may be that you will find shelter”; NRSV “perhaps you may be hidden.”

verses.zh: 迦萨必致见弃；亚实基伦必然荒凉。人在正午必赶出亚实突的民；以革伦也被拔出根来。
verses.en: Indeed,[NOTE:1] Gaza will be deserted[NOTE:2] and Ashkelon will become a heap of ruins.[NOTE:3] Invaders will drive away the people of Ashdod by noon,[NOTE:4] and Ekron will be overthrown.[NOTE:5]
notes: Or “for” (KJV, NAB, NASB, NRSV).
There is a sound play here in the Hebrew text: the name Gaza (עַזָּה, ’azzah) sounds like the word translated “deserted” (עֲזוּבָה, ’azuvah).
Or “a desolate place.”
Heb “[As for] Ashdod, at noon they will drive her away.”sn The reference to noon may suggest a sudden, quick defeat (see Jer 6:4; 15:8).
Heb “uprooted.” There is a sound play here in the Hebrew text: the name “Ekron” (עֶקְרוֹן, ’eqron) sounds like the word translated “uprooted” (תֵּעָקֵר, te’aqer).

verses.zh: 住沿海之地的基利提族有祸了！迦南、非利士人之地啊，耶和华的话与你反对，说：我必毁灭你，以致无人居住。
verses.en: Beware, you who live by the sea, the people who came from Crete.[NOTE:1] The Lord’s message is against you, Canaan, land of the Philistines:“I will destroy everyone who lives there!”[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “Kerethites,” a people settled alongside the Philistines in the coastal areas of southern Palestine (cf. 1 Sam 30:14; Ezek 25:16). They originally came from the island of Crete.
Heb “I will destroy you so there is no inhabitant [remaining].”

verses.zh: 沿海之地要变为草场，其上有牧人的住处和羊群的圈。
verses.en: The seacoast[NOTE:1] will be used as pasture lands[NOTE:2] by the shepherdsand as pens for their flocks.
notes: The NIV84 here supplies the phrase “where the Kerethites dwell” (“Kerethites” is translated in v. 5 as “the people who came from Crete”) as an interpretive gloss, but this phrase is not in the MT. The NAB likewise reads “the coastland of the Cretans,” supplying “Cretans” here.

The Hebrew phrase here is נְוֹת כְּרֹת (nevot kerot). The first word is probably a plural form of נָוָה (navah, “pasture”). The meaning of the second word is unclear. It may be a synonym of the preceding word (cf. NRSV “pastures, meadows for shepherds”); there is a word כַּר (kar, “pasture”) in biblical Hebrew, but elsewhere it forms its plural with a masculine ending. Some have suggested the meaning “wells” or “caves” used as shelters (cf. NEB “shepherds’ huts”); in this case, one might translate, “The seacoast will be used for pasturelands; for shepherds’ wells/caves” (cf. NIV11 “the land by the sea will become pastures having wells for shepherds”).

verses.zh: 这地必为犹大家剩下的人所得；他们必在那里牧放群羊，晚上必躺卧在亚实基伦的房屋中；因为耶和华―他们的　神必眷顾他们，使他们被掳的人归回。
verses.en: Those who are left from the kingdom of Judah[NOTE:1] will take possession of it.[NOTE:2] By the sea[NOTE:3] they[NOTE:4] will graze,in the houses of Ashkelon they will lie down in the evening,for the Lord their God will intervene for them[NOTE:5] and restore their prosperity.[NOTE:6]
notes: Heb “the remnant of the house of Judah.”
Or “the coast will belong to the remnant of the house of Judah.”

Heb “on them.” But there is no clear antecedent to match the masculine plural pronoun. It is preferable to emend the text from עֲלֵיהֶם (ʿalehem) to עַל־הַיָּם (ʿal hayyam, “by the sea”). This emendation assumes a transposition of letters and then an improper word division in the MT (cf. NEB “They shall pasture their flocks by the sea”). See J. J. M. Roberts, Nahum, Habakkuk, and Zephaniah (OTL), 192.

The referent of the pronominal subject (“they”) is unclear. It may refer (1) to the shepherds (in which case the first verb should be translated, “pasture their sheep,” cf. NEB), or (2) to the Judahites occupying the area, who are being compared to sheep (cf. NIV, “there they will find pasture”).
Or “will care for them.”

Traditionally, “restore their captivity,” i.e., bring back their captives. This followed the understanding of the LXX and other versions (cf. KJV “turn away their captivity”). The Hebrew tradition is mixed, the consonantal text implies the reading שְׁבוּת (shevut) but it is vocalized as if שְׁבִית (shevit). It is more likely the noun means “fortunes” (HALOT 1386 s.v. שְׁבִית, שְׁבוּת) as in the expression “restore their fortunes” (cf. NEB, NASB, NIV, NRSV).

verses.zh: 我听见摩押人的毁谤和亚扪人的辱骂，就是毁谤我的百姓，自夸自大，侵犯他们的境界。
verses.en: “I have heard Moab’s tauntsand the Ammonites’ insults.They[NOTE:1] taunted my peopleand verbally harassed those living in Judah.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “who.” A new sentence was begun here in the translation for stylistic reasons.

Heb “and they made great [their mouth?] against their territory.” Other possible translation options include (1) “they enlarged their own territory” (cf. NEB) and (2) “they bragged about [the size] of their own territory.”

verses.zh: 万军之耶和华―以色列的　神说：我指着我的永生起誓：摩押必像所多玛，亚扪人必像蛾摩拉，都变为刺草、盐坑、永远荒废之地。我百姓所剩下的必掳掠他们；我国中所余剩的必得着他们的地。
verses.en: Therefore, as surely as I live,” says the Lord of Heaven’s Armies, the God of Israel,“be certain that Moab will become like Sodomand the Ammonites like Gomorrah.They will be overrun by weeds,[NOTE:1] filled with salt pits,[NOTE:2] and permanently desolate.Those of my people who are left[NOTE:3] will plunder their belongings;[NOTE:4] those who are left in Judah[NOTE:5] will take possession of their land.”
notes: The Hebrew text reads מִמְשַׁק חָרוּל (mimshaq kharul, “[?] of weeds”). The meaning of the first word is unknown. The present translation (“They will be overrun by weeds”) is speculative, based on the general sense of the context. For a defense of “overrun” on linguistic grounds, see R. D. Patterson, Nahum, Habakkuk, Zephaniah (WEC), 347. Cf. NEB “a pile of weeds”; NIV “a place of weeds”; NRSV “a land possessed by nettles.”

The Hebrew text reads וּמִכְרֵה־מֶלַח (umikhreh melakh, “and a [?] of salt”). The meaning of the first word is unclear, though “pit” (NASB, NIV, NRSV; NKJV “saltpit”), “mine,” and “heap” (cf. NEB “a rotting heap of saltwort”) are all options. The words “filled with” are supplied for clarification.
Or “The remnant of my people.”
Heb “them.” The actual object of the plundering, “their belongings,” has been specified in the translation for clarity.
Heb “[the] nation.” For clarity the “nation” has been specified as “Judah” in the translation.

verses.zh: 这事临到他们是因他们骄傲，自夸自大，毁谤万军之耶和华的百姓。
verses.en: This is how they will be repaid for their arrogance,[NOTE:1] for they taunted and verbally harassed[NOTE:2] the people of the Lord of Heaven’s Armies.
notes: Heb “this is for them in place of their arrogance.”
Heb “made great [their mouth?] against” (cf. the last phrase of v. 8).

verses.zh: 耶和华必向他们显可畏之威，因他必叫世上的诸神瘦弱。列国海岛的居民各在自己的地方敬拜他。
verses.en: The Lord will terrify them,[NOTE:1] for[NOTE:2] he will weaken[NOTE:3] all the gods of the earth.All the distant nations will worship the Lord in their own lands.[NOTE:4]
notes: Heb “will be awesome over [or, “against”] them.”
Or “certainly.”

The meaning of this rare Hebrew word is unclear. If the meaning is indeed “weaken,” then this line may be referring to the reduction of these gods’ territory through conquest (see Adele Berlin, Zephaniah [AB 25A], 110-11). Cf. NEB “reduce to beggary”; NASB “starve”; NIV “when he destroys”; NRSV “shrivel.”
Heb “and all the coastlands of the nations will worship [or, “bow down”] to him, each from his own place.”

verses.zh: 古实人哪，你们必被我的刀所杀。
verses.en: “You[NOTE:1] Ethiopians[NOTE:2] will also die by my sword!”[NOTE:3]
notes: Though there is no formal introduction, these words are apparently spoken by the Lord (note my sword).

Heb “Cushites.” This is traditionally assumed to refer to people from the region south of Egypt, i.e., Nubia or northern Sudan, referred to as “Ethiopia” by classical authors (not the more recent Abyssinia).
Heb “Also you Cushites, who lie dead by my sword.”

verses.zh: 耶和华必伸手攻击北方，毁灭亚述，使尼尼微荒凉，又干旱如旷野。
verses.en: The Lord[NOTE:1] will attack the north[NOTE:2] and destroy Assyria.He will make Nineveh a heap of ruins;it will be as barren[NOTE:3] as the desert.
notes: Heb “He”; the referent (the Lord) has been specified in the translation for clarity.
Heb “he will stretch out his hand against the north.”
Or “dry.”

verses.zh: 群畜，就是各国（国：或译类）的走兽必卧在其中；鹈鹕和箭猪要宿在柱顶上。在窗户内有鸣叫的声音；门槛都必毁坏，香柏木已经露出。
verses.en: Flocks and herds[NOTE:1] will lie down in the middle of it,as well as every kind of wild animal.[NOTE:2] Owls[NOTE:3] will sleep in the tops of its support pillars;they will hoot through the windows.[NOTE:4] Rubble will cover the thresholds;[NOTE:5] even the cedar work[NOTE:6] will be exposed to the elements.[NOTE:7]
notes: Heb “flocks.” The Hebrew word can refer to both flocks of sheep and herds of cattle.

Heb “[and] all the wild animals of a nation.” How גוֹי (goy, “nation”) relates to what precedes is unclear. It may be an unusual expression or need emendation to another word. See J. J. M. Roberts, Nahum, Habakkuk, and Zephaniah (OTL), 193.

The Hebrew text reads here גַּם־קָאַת גַּם־קִפֹּד (gam qaʾat gam qippod). The term קָאַת refers to some type of bird (see Lev 11:18; Deut 14:17) that was typically found near ruins (Isa 34:11); one of the most common translations is “owl” (cf. NEB “horned owl”; NIV, NRSV “desert owl”; contra NASB “pelican”). The term קִפֹּד may also refer to a type of bird (cf. NEB “ruffed bustard”; NIV, NRSV “screech owl”). Some suggest a rodent may be in view (cf. NASB “hedgehog”); this is not unreasonable, for a rodent or some other small animal would be able to sleep in the tops of pillars which would be lying in the ruins of the fallen buildings.
Heb “a sound will sing in the window.” If some type of owl is in view, “hoot” is a more appropriate translation (cf. NEB, NRSV).

Heb “rubble [will be] on the threshold.” “Rubble” translates the Hebrew word חֹרֶב (khorev, “desolation”). Some emend to עֹרֵב (ʿorev, “raven”) following the LXX and Vulgate; Adele Berlin translates, “A voice shall shriek from the window—a raven at the sill” (Zephaniah [AB 25A], 104).
The meaning of the Hebrew word translated “cedar work” (so NASB, NRSV) is unclear; NIV has “the beams of cedar.”
Heb “one will expose.” The subject is probably indefinite, though one could translate, “for he [i.e., God] will lay bare.”

verses.zh: 这是素来欢乐安然居住的城，心里说：惟有我，除我以外再没有别的；现在何竟荒凉成为野兽躺卧之处！凡经过的人都必摇手嗤笑她。
verses.en: This is how the once-proud city will end up—the city that was so secure.[NOTE:1] She thought to herself,[NOTE:2] “I am unique! No one can compare to me!”[NOTE:3] What a heap of ruins she has become, a place where wild animals live!Everyone who passes by her taunts her[NOTE:4] and shakes his fist.[NOTE:5]
notes: Heb “This is the proud city, the one that lives securely.” “This” refers to the previous description of how the city will turn out.
Heb “the one who says in her heart [or mind].”
Heb “I [am], and besides me there is no other.”
Heb “hisses”; or “whistles.”
Hissing (or whistling) and shaking the fist were apparently ways of taunting a defeated foe or an object of derision in the culture of the time.
